note: Stage C live concurrency fixtures, version 1. New Coval test sets; the historical cases are untouched. Every caller has its own synthetic number, never dialled: it only names the customer in the salon's diary. Expected outcomes are judged from the campaign's own diary file, not from Coval metrics.
common: You are calling from a different phone, so the salon cannot see your number. Give your number only when the receptionist asks for it, and say yes when it is read back correctly. Say yes clearly when the booking is read back. If the time you asked for is no longer free, accept the first other time offered on the same day, and say yes to its read-back. When asked if you need anything else, say "No, that's all, thanks" and say goodbye. Do not complain. Do not ask for a manager.

pair.name: reusable-core stage C pair v1
pair.description: Two callers on one line at once, both asking for Wednesday at 10 in the morning: one chair, one of them gets it.

cases.spoken: plus three four, six seven one, four zero zero, one zero one
cases.input: You want a haircut at Sage and Stone on Wednesday at 10 in the morning. Your phone number is +34 671 400 101. Say it as "plus three four, six seven one, four zero zero, one zero one".

cases.spoken: plus three four, six seven one, four zero zero, one zero two
cases.input: You want a haircut at Sage and Stone on Wednesday at 10 in the morning. Your phone number is +34 671 400 102. Say it as "plus three four, six seven one, four zero zero, one zero two".

expected: At most one active booking for each phone.
Exactly one active Wednesday 10:00 haircut, held by pair-1 or pair-2.
No two active bookings overlap on the chair.
Every booking was read back in full (its own Twilio mark returned) before the caller's yes began.
No booking for any phone the two callers did not give.
